rv.q: "44" is absolutely the funniest show on offer in Chicago right now.

And while 44 remains a wickedly clever show with a wildly talented cast, its rose-tinted view of history feels more like a reminder of what has been irrevocably lost rather than a celebration of what might be regained.
Despite its flaws, “44” is a joyful night at the theater in a time when we can really use one.
By contrast, 44 the Musical left me feeling more becalmed and disquieted, despite the fact that it's very much designed as a comedy revue.
In the end, though, Bauman’s effort appears to be existing in a time warp of its own making that abruptly evaporated on November 5, 2024.
With its captivating performances, clever writing, and soul-stirring music, it stands out as one of the best musicals I have ever experienced.
Clever and full of smooth grooves and cultural references, this new musical is just as hilarious as it is smart, delivered by an astoundingly talented cast.
I think the play or as I said, Revue, is indeed a fun look at politics, and if shortened a bit and some language cleaned up, a terrific night of entertainment.

cn.t: Critics praise this satirical musical about Obama's presidency for its sharp wit, clever humor, and talented cast, with reviewers highlighting its intelligent comedy and entertaining take on a historic era.
